feed.title: The Civic Bestiary - latest
feed.subtitle: New entries, and notes on the ones already in the guide.

entry.title: Three ways of not answering
entry.summary: I wasn't told, I cannot be made to say, and the question never got asked properly: three moves for the three ways of not answering.
entry.content:
Three moves, one idea. Unawares is I was not told. Plead the Fifth is I cannot be made to say. Depositioning is the question never got asked properly. They file in chapter III because they are the same character in three costumes, and because that chapter was the thinnest in the book and the one most in need of the vocabulary of the non-answer.

The Fifth is the entry to read carefully. The privilege is real, it is old, and the guide is not against it. The move is what the right becomes when it is the only sentence in the answer, offered in a hearing where what is at stake is a headline, not a cell.

Each carries a source: plausible deniability, the amendment itself, and Rule 30 on depositions. Each is also wired to the thing it answers. The subpoena now points at both moves that meet it, and the secret meeting at the move that hides inside it, because a reader who finds one half of a mechanism should be able to reach the other from the page.

Chapter III has the vocabulary it was missing. It is still the shortest chapter, and it is no longer the least useful.

entry.title: What a polish pass finds
entry.summary: Nothing structural, which is the interesting part. The shape of the guide was sound and the drift was in the sentences.
entry.content:
We walked every record against the contract, expecting to find broken entries and finding none. What the pass turned up instead was drift: three records written in a register the other 192 do not use, eight links that rendered nowhere, and three sightings that never named the thing they were sighting.

The voice problem is the one worth writing down. Crookmaxxing, JAQing Off and Bootcurious carried part-of-speech markers inside their senses, in italics, and a long explanatory clause where the book uses an epigram. The part of speech already has a field. The senses now open the way the rest of their kind opens, and Bootcurious stopped describing a person when it is filed as a condition that expires.

The dead links are the failure this guide is most likely to have. Eight records listed a term under both the related list and the confused-with pair. Both generators drop the twin from the related list, because the pair edge already renders it, so the link was authored, validated, and shown to nobody. A rule enforced in two places is a rule that eventually gets satisfied in neither.

The graph had drifted too. The transcript was named in the counter prose of Heckler's veto and Rally and was not wired to either, so the page told you to publish the transcript and did not offer you the entry that says how. Both edges are in now, and Rally no longer claims a habitat commits a fallacy it merely houses.

A polish pass is not a feature. It is the maintenance that keeps a field guide usable after a hundred small additions, and the finding is always the same: the entries are fine, the joins are where it rots.

The joins are also where the sibling tool starts. tresridge is the same discipline pointed at a .tres tree: it reads the families and the edges you already have, names what dangles and what nobody declared, and only then asks you to write the declaration. One gate in CI, exit 0 or 1, no prose to parse. The audit behind this post is the manual version: read the graph, find the references that go nowhere, fix them, make the fix a rule. tresridge is what that walk looks like when the tree is too large to walk.

entry.title: Three words that end an argument
entry.summary: The claim, the label, and the password: three species that use a word to close a question instead of answering it.
entry.content:
Three species arrived in one sitting and they share a job: a word that does the work of an argument. Ricochetoric fires a claim and lets the answer bounce off it. Ismatic is the label that ends the sentence before the sentence reaches the evidence. Shibbolether is the password that tells you which side of the line someone stands on.

What separates them is what the word is for. The ricochetoric wants you to answer the claim. The ismatic wants you to answer for the label. The shibbolether wants you to say the word. One is a projectile, one is a verdict, one is a test, and a reader who cannot tell them apart will use the wrong name on the wrong person, which is the failure this guide exists to prevent.

All three are filed in chapter II, beside the moves they borrow from, and each carries the tell that separates it from its nearest neighbour. The counters are the useful part: ask for the claim behind the label, ask who is testing whom, and answer the projectile with the question it was avoiding.

entry.title: How a remedy gets captured
entry.summary: Three remedies that assume the other side cares what the record says, and five entries about making a thing normal first.
entry.content:
Chapter VI closed with three remedies about the far side of a remedy. The reserve puts supply on the market to break a leverage play. The sponsor line names who paid for the advertisement. The withdrawal clause makes leaving a procedure rather than an announcement.

All three assume the other party cares what the record says. That is the difference between a remedy and a hope, and the chapter is honest about it, because every entry in it carries its failure mode. A reserve can be sold off. A sponsor line can be routed through a name. A withdrawal clause can be triggered by the side that wanted out.

The other five entries arrived in the same round, and they are chapter V's machinery of respectability. Industry conference is the room where a practice becomes respectable. Soft launch ships the contested change with no speech and a line on a form. Grandfather clause exempts what is already there. Outrage fatigue is the audience having spent its capacity to be shocked. Precedentarian treats the last decision as the decision.

Read together they are one sentence: nothing has to be defended if it can be made normal first.

A remedy that assumes good faith is a test of it.

entry.title: The policy turn
entry.summary: Thirteen entries, six of them capabilities of a body rather than habits of a person.
entry.content:
Thirteen entries, and six of them are the same kind: capabilities of an institution. Citizens United holds that spending is speech. Forever war continues because the alternative is a vote. Oil diplomacy conducts foreign policy by supply. Breaking treaties treats an accord as a policy preference. Lobbyism is the system in which the regulated write the regulation, and WMD mongering sells a war with a threat nobody can see.

That is a different animal from a species. A species is a pattern a person wears. An ability belongs to a body, an office, or a machine, and no single person owns it. The guide's most uncomfortable claim lives in that difference: the most damaging moves are legal, and they belong to entities rather than to anybody you can point at.

The rest of the round is the furniture around it. PAC check is the condition of being funded. Unelected official is governing without a ballot. Good ol' boys club is the room where the decision is made by people who already know each other, and secret meeting is the room where it was decided before the meeting where it was announced.

Two moves finish it. Good cop, bad cop presents one position twice, once as a threat and once as a kindness, so the second sounds like a concession. Vague promises commits to nothing in the grammar of commitment.

A field guide to characters can stop at the characters. This is the round where it stopped being able to.

entry.title: Chapter V gets a cast
entry.summary: The chapter about normalization had an appendix and no characters. Now it has two, and four ways of missing the drift.
entry.content:
Chapter V is about normalization, and until this afternoon it had no cast. The chapter had an appendix of fallacies and nothing at the front of the book: no species, nobody to point at. Then Passoffist and Provocrop went in at positions one and two.

Passoffist keeps a subject off the table while looking fair about it: the topic changed, the link not opened, the question answered with the process for answering it. Provocrop carries the provocation as merchandise: the slogan on the chest, the flag on the truck, the insult on the bumper.

Four fallacies followed, and all four are about a baseline that moves. Creeping normality accepts each small change because it is small. Shifting baseline judges the present against the last generation's memory instead of the record. Normalcy bias reads the absence of disaster as evidence against it. Just-world hypothesis explains suffering by the character of the sufferer.

That is the chapter in one round: a person who moves the line, a person who wears the line, and four ways of not noticing that it moved.

A chapter with no cast is a chapter nobody can be found in.

entry.title: One word, filed alone
entry.summary: One entry, one merge: Critizen, the pattern of treating a shared obligation as something that binds other people.
entry.content:
The word is Critizen, and the pattern is the tax refused on a theory, the summons answered late, the rule that is real because somebody else is following it.

It is the only entry this guide has ever added alone, in a round of its own. That is an accident of the afternoon rather than a policy, but the shape of the file is worth saying out loud: one word, one merge, one line in the log.

It could not wait for company, because it names the failure that makes every remedy expensive. A remedy depends on the obligation being general. The critizen has read the statute and decided it is a description of other people.

A guide adds what it noticed. Some days that is sixteen entries and a room. Some days it is one word.

entry.title: Chapter VI outgrows the ballot
entry.summary: The chapter opened with the polling place and had a courtroom by lunchtime.
entry.content:
Chapter VI opened with the polling place: the clerk, the poll worker, the count. Two rounds later it had a courtroom. Cross-examination, notice and comment, recusal, the stay, and the offices that make them real: the juror, the ombudsman, the public defender, the statistician, the translator.

The two hardest arrived last. The carve-out is the statutory exception that removes a contract term's power over one kind of dispute: the silence clause that cannot reach a case of assault. The redistricting commission draws the districts outside the legislature, with a fixed membership, published criteria, and draft maps.

The chapter's argument, made twice: a remedy needs a forum. Cross-examination is a technique, and it is nothing without a juror who was instructed and a judge who excludes. Notice and comment is a procedure, and it is nothing without a record a court can review. Filing the technique beside the office is the whole point of the chapter.

The statistician and the translator are the two people forget. A count nobody can audit and a rule nobody can read are the same failure at different distances: the institution produced a number or a sentence, and nobody outside it can tell whether either is true.

The chapter outgrew the ballot in an afternoon. That is what an honest taxonomy does: the next entry tells you what the category was missing.

entry.title: A second sighting
entry.summary: Seven fallacies went into the reference end, and every fallacy already there got a second entry wired to it.
entry.content:
The seven are Kafka trap, Bulverism, McNamara fallacy, Nirvana fallacy, base rate fallacy, appeal to force, the fallacy fallacy. The same pass went back over the ones already filed and gave each a second sighting, a second entry that commits it in the wild.

The rule that forced the sweep: a fallacy filed on one sighting cannot be told apart from the habit of the entry that produced it. Two sightings is the smallest evidence that a move is portable, and a guide that keeps the rule can be checked from outside, because the graph either has the second edge or it does not. Every fallacy now carries at least two, so a reader can walk from the fallacy to the things that commit it instead of taking the entry's word for the pattern.

Three of the seven are the same trick at different distances. The Kafka trap makes the denial into the evidence. Bulverism answers the argument by explaining the arguer. The fallacy fallacy takes one bad argument as proof that the claim is false. All three end the argument without touching it.

The other four are about what gets weighed. McNamara counts what can be counted and files the rest as commentary. Nirvana compares a proposal to nothing and the present arrangement to nothing, so only the proposal looks expensive. The base rate fallacy weighs one vivid instance against the frequency it came from. Appeal to force prices the dissent before the merits are weighed at all.

A guide is only as good as its sightings. Two is the smallest number that is not an anecdote.

entry.title: Chapter VI answers the creatures
entry.summary: Five chapters name the failures. The sixth names the people who catch them, and the procedures that need no office at all.
entry.content:
A field guide that starts prescribing becomes a pamphlet, so the first five chapters only diagnose: name the creature, the move, the habitat, and stop there. Chapter VI breaks that rule on purpose. It is the first chapter whose entries are the answer rather than the description of the problem.

The keystones are offices. The clerk keeps the body's memory, the agenda, the roll call, the motions as adopted rather than as proposed. The poll worker runs the count everyone else argues about afterwards. The archivist keeps what nobody has asked for yet. The librarian holds the shelf the feed cannot sort. The caseworker reads the file. The editor decides what a sentence is allowed to mean. The moderator holds the line the heckler's veto is built to cross. The auditor follows the fee. Eight of them, each filed with a tell and a counter like any creature, because an office is exactly as easy to hollow out as a person.

The remedies are the ones available to somebody with no office at all: records request, lateral reading, the second source, the steelman, the transcript, the written reason, the public count, random draw, fee shift, sunset clause, the audit. Each is written as an instruction rather than a description. Read one out loud and you can run it tomorrow.

The split is the argument. A remedy without an office is advice. An office without a remedy is a title. Filing both in one chapter lets the guide say what a body needs and who is supposed to be holding it, and lets a reader see the gap when the answer is nobody.

Five chapters describe how a body loses the thread. This one describes the people who keep the receipts.

entry.title: The procedural layer
entry.summary: Fifteen entries that are not habits. They are the machinery that makes the habit affordable.
entry.content:
Fifteen entries, and the tone changes. SLAPP is a suit filed not to win but to cost. Qualified immunity shields an official unless the right was clearly established at the time. NDA converts a fact into a liability. None of these is a personality. They are the machinery that makes the personality affordable.

Half the round is that machinery, and the other half is the machinery that can still close the gap. Cloture closes debate. Discharge petition escapes a committee that will not report. Consent decree turns a settlement into an order a judge enforces. Judge shopping is the same procedure used from the other end: file where the bench is favourable.

Four moves need a crowd. Astroturfing manufactures one, flood the zone drowns it, motte hop retreats inside it, and the heckler's veto makes speaking impossible rather than answering. Two habitats stage it: the perp walk before a jury has been chosen, and the pseudo-event that exists in order to be covered.

Two conditions finish the list, and both are about standing. Access is being allowed in: the interview, the background call, the standing that makes a question possible. A hot mic is the same standing without the control.

A guide that only names the creature is a list of insults. The procedural layer is what makes it usable, because a mechanism has a name and a name can be argued with.

entry.title: The room and the calendar
entry.summary: Sixteen entries, and the first thing to notice is how many of them are rooms.
entry.content:
Sixteen entries, and the first thing to notice is how many are rooms. A rally, a briefing room, a spin room. The first day had already filed the media habitats, the cable panel and the comment section and the group chat. This round filed the rooms the government owns, where the press is invited in and the answer is performed.

The second thing to notice is the calendar. Lame duck is an officeholder whose replacement is already elected: the powers intact, the consequences gone. Convention bounce is four days of unchallenged messaging and a sample. Frankincense is the franking privilege, mail that travels free because the office sent it.

Then the calendar as a weapon. Friday news dump releases the inconvenient thing when the reporters who would ask are off. Dead cat puts something so shocking on the table that the table has to be about it. Trial balloon leaks the proposal to see whether it survives, and push poll dresses a smear as a survey.

The quiet five are procedural. Blueslip, nightdocket, pocketveto, recessure, signaway: five ways a signature, a calendar, or a committee can decide what a debate was supposed to decide.

A habitat is not scenery. It is the reason the same creature says a different thing in a different room. The guide had the creatures. This round gave them somewhere to be found.
